name: Manipur
blurb: A bowl-shaped valley ringed by hills, Manipur's Meitei culture centres on the historic seat of its kings and one of India's only all-women-run marketplaces.

districts.name: Imphal West
districts.blurb: The heart of the Manipur valley, centred on the historic royal seat of Kangla.

places.name: Kangla Fort
places.blurb: The moated historic seat of Manipur's Meitei kings, spiritual heart of the state, held by colonial forces for over a century before its return in 2004.
places.bestPhoto: The Kangla Sha sculptures against the moat at golden hour
places.history: The historic seat of Manipur's Meitei kings, Kangla was the royal capital and religious centre for centuries until the mid-18th century relocation of the palace. It was occupied by British forces after the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891 and was only handed back to the state in 2004.
places.architecture: A moated complex containing palace ruins, temples, and the Kangla Sha — a pair of mythical dragon-lion sculptures considered a symbol of Manipur — alongside earthen ramparts and gateways.

timeline.label: British forces occupy Kangla Fort after the Anglo-Manipur War.
The fort is formally handed back to the Manipur state government.

facts: Occupied by the Assam Rifles for over a century before being returned to civilian control.
The Kangla Sha dragon-lion motif appears widely across Manipuri state symbolism today.
Considered the spiritual heart of the Meitei people.
hiddenGems: Ima Keithel ("Mother's Market"), an all-women-run market in central Imphal
Loktak Lake and its floating phumdi islands, a short drive away
food: Manipuri thali with eromba and singju
Local rice beer traditions in nearby villages
experiences: Heritage walk through the fort ramparts and moat

travel.railway: No direct rail; nearest is Dimapur, ~215 km
travel.tip: Combine with a visit to Ima Keithel market in the same day — both sit centrally in Imphal.
